turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you doing right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm selling some handmade earrings online and my photos look so amateur.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Small jewellery is tricky, but very doable at home. Do you have a window that gets bright, indirect light?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, the spare room. No direct sun.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect. Put a sheet of white card under the earrings and another one bent up behind them, so you get a clean seamless background.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Almost. Get close, tap on the earring to focus, and use a tiny bit of putty to stand them upright so they catch the light.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They're quite sparkly. Will that be a problem?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sparkle is good, glare isn't. A piece of white paper on the window side softens it. Take one photo on an ear or a hand too, so people see the size.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, that's a really good point, people always ask how big they are.
